summary:
I've been building a module that connects a D&D campaign app of mine to Foundry, and it's now public. The part that shaped the design: Foundry sends GM-only documents to every player's browser, so anything hidden stays in my app until the DM reveals it. I tested it inside a real Foundry install, which turned up a bug the unit tests couldn't. Foundry edits the objects you pass to its create calls in place, so my code was reading fields that had already been deleted. The final run passed 27 of 27 checks, and releases ship as a single squashed commit after a leak scan.

The same app got an import feature for adventures. You paste in a book you own, it proposes NPCs, monsters, store items and a beat list, and the source text is deleted once you've reviewed and applied the result. I then added photo input and ran the same three pages through two models. Haiku made four silent wrong values, in table cells and a dice count, and never flagged one as illegible. Sonnet made none. It costs a few cents a page instead of about one, and I took the cost. Anthropic's content filter also refuses to transcribe published prose, so photos are for homebrew, tables and stat blocks, and the UI says so.

On the GPU side, Switchboard is the small proxy that lets ComfyUI and several local language models take turns on one 16 GB card. Two things bit me this month. If anything else holds a GPU lease under the wrong client name, Switchboard evicts ComfyUI as "everyone else". ComfyUI then blocks inside its own event loop and the whole server goes quiet until the lease times out. Separately, adding `--no-mmap` to the model launchers took cold generation from 4.6 to 32 tokens a second, because experts were paging off disk mid-token.

Smaller items: a realtime bug where about ten components shared one channel per campaign, so closing any one of them silently cut live updates for the whole page. I also spent a day on an inference engine experiment that ended in a dead end. The card is too old for the compiler to build the kernels it needs, and more RAM wasn't going to fix that. I cleaned up and moved on.

highlights.oneLiner: Found a stray lease made the proxy evict ComfyUI and hang it until timeout.
Renders hold the shared GPU through a lease; one bad client name froze it.
Added power counters to internal fleet monitoring; one box is 85% of draw.
Agent brain now loads fully into RAM; cold generation went 4.6 to 32 tok/s.
